A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AASD research. All 13 pages of each version, including equations, tables, figures, and appendices, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original generation-quality and decoding-efficiency experiments, component ablations, threshold sensitivity results, and a case study.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds model-judged response comparisons, batch-size efficiency measurements, and comparative response cases.

M1.justification: Context-aware drafting, alignment sampling, entropy-based conditional verification, and draft-pool updating are unchanged. Section 3 and Appendix C's Algorithm 1 retain the same procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same eight QA, summarization, and code-completion datasets and the same SpecBench tasks. The added judging and batch-size experiments reuse existing coverage.

E2.justification: The sampling baselines, ARD/REST/PLD efficiency comparisons, and large/small-model speculative-decoding comparisons are retained. DeepSeek-V3 is introduced as an evaluator, not a competing decoding method; greedy sampling was already evaluated.

E3.justification: v2 adds DeepSeek-V3 judging with greedy-win, tie, and AASD-win rates in Table 3, plus SpecBench evaluation at batch sizes 1, 2, 4, and 8 in Appendix D. Existing splits, metrics, generation models, and decoding settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix D adds batch-size sensitivity analysis, and Appendix E adds selected cases illustrating three error patterns. Existing component ablations, threshold sweeps, overlap analysis, and the original threshold-dependent case study are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version supplies repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new win/tie percentages and batch-size results are point estimates without added uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Previously reported numerical results remain unchanged. New Table 3 reports more AASD wins than greedy wins on six datasets, with the reverse on TQA and GovReport. Table 9 adds speedups of 1.83, 1.65, 1.60, and 0.96 at batch sizes 1, 2, 4, and 8; Figure 6 adds three qualitative response comparisons.

T1.justification: Equations 1–7, including the draft-tree definition, entropy-based verification threshold, and source-target overlap ratio, are unchanged. No new formal assumptions, theorems, derivations, or proofs appear.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same training-free alignment-sampling and conditional-verification contributions. The headline approximately 3.3-point quality gain, 2.39 mean acceptance length, and 2.23-fold speedup are unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix D now explicitly limits observed acceleration to batch sizes up to four in the tested environment. Appendix E characterizes selected improvements through textual infidelity, overcautious refusal, and language inconsistency. Existing threshold and harmful-context limitations remain.

D1.justification: Implementation documentation retains the six-token n-grams and retrieval keys, alpha/beta settings, two-token expansion cap, four A100-40GB GPUs, and pseudocode. Beyond the new evaluation settings, v2 adds no implementation instructions, judge prompts, or code/data access information.

R1.justification: v2 adds the DeepSeek-V3 technical-report citation to identify its new evaluator. The related-work discussion and positioning against earlier speculative-decoding and context-utilization methods are otherwise unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 adds an affiliation, acknowledgments, a short neural-evaluation paragraph, and Appendices D–E, alongside small spelling and capitalization corrections. The existing narrative and section organization are largely retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 3 and 9 and Figure 6. Existing Tables 3–7 become Tables 4–8 and several displays move, including the overlap table moving above Figure 5. Retained figures and table structures are otherwise unchanged.

improvement.justification: The added model-judged comparison and concrete response cases modestly strengthen the evidence beyond automatic scores. Appendix D usefully exposes loss of acceleration at batch size eight, clarifying practical applicability. The judging protocol remains briefly specified and new results lack uncertainty estimates, limiting the gain; the core method and original results are unchanged.
